hook.text: Apple's first iPhone had no buttons. In 2007, that was shocking. Surprise made the product unforgettable.

buildup.text: Design theorist Don Norman calls delightful surprises 'emotional design'—objects that make you feel something.

discovery.text: Easter eggs in software—hidden features—create micro-surprises that build brand loyalty and user delight.

twist.text: Surprise in UX must be careful. An unexpected popup annoys; an unexpected shortcut delights. Context decides.

climax.text: The best designs feel surprising the first time and inevitable every time after. That's the hallmark of great UX.

punchline.text: Great design surprises you once and satisfies you forever.

quiz.question: What did Don Norman call delightful surprises in objects?
